name: Jody Ito
life: “I still remember meeting the first real user of the schedule I designed.” On Monday, near Ferris Deli, Jody asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I wrote the billing software and never watched somebody fasten a row of small buttons.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a faded indigo overshirt and a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. Jody has a straight nose and deep-set eyes, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Jody counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices during a conversation.
personality: Jody has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Jody knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To watch a full dressing visit before revising the software.
family: Evan Koch is Jody’s cousin raised in the same household. Jody brings a spare shopping bag. Evan chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A closing hour*, Evan says, “I work next door and hear the spinners every day.”
connections: Jasmine Boyd. The stopwatch and the billing software meet a person who laughs at minute thirteen.

reactions.situation: A visit runs into a second billing block
reactions.response: Jody records the extra time actually spent with the client.

reactions.situation: A neighbor offers to pay for a favor that was meant kindly
reactions.response: Jody accepts a small agreed amount if paying lets the neighbor keep their pride.

reactions.response: Jody asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
